schemes.label: NIP

provenance.sourceText: «Art. 106e. 1. Faktura powinna zawierać: [...] 4) numer, za pomocą którego podatnik jest zidentyfikowany na potrzeby podatku, z zastrzeżeniem pkt 24 lit. a oraz pkt 25;»

schemes.notes: Ustawa z dnia 11 marca 2004 r. o podatku od towarów i usług, art. 106e ust. 1 pkt 4 — read as the official consolidated text (tekst jednolity) at Dz.U. 2025 poz. 775 (Obwieszczenie Marszałka Sejmu RP z dnia 21 maja 2025 r.), fetched directly as a PDF from dziennikustaw.gov.pl (https://dziennikustaw.gov.pl/D2025000077501.pdf, landing page https://dziennikustaw.gov.pl/DU/rok/2025/pozycja/775), curl then `pdftotext -layout`, 2026-09-13 — isap.sejm.gov.pl was not used (sits behind Incapsula bot protection). This binds the SELLER (`podatnik`, the taxpayer issuing the invoice) and is required on every invoice except two narrow, non-waiving substitutions: pkt 24 lit. a (a PL-prefixed number for one triangulation-type intra-EU case) and pkt 25 (an EX-suffixed cross-border small-business-exemption number, a 2025 addition under art. 113a ust. 1) — neither carve-out removes the requirement, both substitute a differently-formatted identifier for the same slot. There is no exemption for a small/exempt domestic seller comparable to France's or Portugal's franchise-based waiver of the identifier itself. Also confirmed NOT waived by the <=450 zl / 100 EUR simplified-invoice threshold (art. 106e ust. 5 pkt 3 i ust. 6): that threshold omits only the buyer's name/address and price-breakdown detail (pkt 3, 8, 9, 11-14), never the seller's or buyer's identification number — ust. 6 goes further and forbids using the threshold AT ALL for a sale where no buyer number under ust. 1 pkt 5 is stated, i.e. the simplification is designed for the known-buyer case, not as a blanket small-amount exemption from identification. IMPORTANT TEXTUAL POINT: the Act's own text never uses the abbreviation "NIP" anywhere in art. 106e, or (per a full-text search of the whole consolidated text) anywhere in the Act at all — it always uses the phrase quoted above. "NIP" is defined in a SEPARATE statute, ustawa z dnia 13 października 1995 r. o zasadach ewidencji i identyfikacji podatników i płatników (read as the tekst jednolity at Dz.U. 2026 poz. 151, https://dziennikustaw.gov.pl/D2026000015101.pdf, same method, 2026-09-13): its art. 3 ust. 1 assigns NIP to "pozostałych podmiotów podlegających obowiązkowi ewidencyjnemu" (all OTHER — i.e. non-natural-person — entities subject to the registration duty) but PESEL instead to a natural person who is neither a registered active VAT taxpayer nor otherwise required to register (art. 3 ust. 1 pkt 1, ust. 1a). `appliesTo` is therefore deliberately set to `'COMPANY'`, NOT `'BOTH'`: for a COMPANY-record seller, NIP specifically (not PESEL) is what this same identification Act assigns, unconditionally alongside art. 106e's own unconditional seller mandate — but for an INDIVIDUAL-record seller the correct identifier can legally be PESEL instead, a different scheme this catalog does not model at all; labelling this fact "NIP" and applying it to INDIVIDUAL sellers too would be wrong in exactly that case, not merely imprecise. `required` is nonetheless set to `false` at country level, for the SAME structural reason as Italy's own facts (see it.json's file-level notes for the full reasoning, reproduced here briefly): this catalog's `appliesTo` axis is consumed identically by the SELLER call-sites (`onboarding.tsx`/`company.settings.tsx`, always `partyType: "COMPANY"`) and the BUYER call-site (`client-upsert.tsx`, `partyType` from the client's own record type), with `required: true` enforced as a real hard save-block in all three. Poland's BUYER-side rule (art. 106e ust. 1 pkt 5) is genuinely conditional — quoted here for completeness: «5) numer, za pomocą którego nabywca towarów lub usług jest zidentyfikowany na potrzeby podatku lub podatku od wartości dodanej, pod którym otrzymał on towary lub usługi, z zastrzeżeniem pkt 24 lit. b;» — self-limiting by its own wording rather than carved out by a numbered exception: it only obligates stating the buyer's number when the buyer actually HAS one and used it to receive the supply; a private consumer simply has no such number to state, so the obligation has no object for that buyer, not because a waiver applies. This is a materially different drafting technique from Italy's (which names Codice Fiscale as an explicit alternative document) but reaches the same practical conclusion this catalog must respect: the buyer's own NIP cannot be safely marked `required: true` here either, so — exactly as for Italy — a single `required` value cannot honestly serve both the seller's unconditional duty and the buyer's conditional one, and `false` is the value that never risks refusing a lawful save. What a resolutionNote-style fix would need: a way to ask whether a given party is itself a registered VAT taxpayer (or, on the seller side, whether an INDIVIDUAL seller is VAT-registered/cash-register-using — the PESEL/NIP switch above) — the same missing axis this task's report names for Italy. No separate `unverified` fact is added for this buyer-side half, unlike Italy's Codice Fiscale: Poland has no second, distinctly-named identifier scheme to host it under (the buyer's number, when owed at all, IS the same NIP already modeled here) — the conditional buyer-side position is instead documented here, in this fact's own `notes`, and in this file's own top-level `notes` below, rather than invented as a second scheme entry with nothing new to say. REGON and KRS (art. 96b ust. 1 i ust. 3 pkt 3 i 5 — the public "wykaz podatników VAT" the tax administration publishes, a completely different provision from art. 106e) are established NOT to be invoice-content requirements at all: a full-text search of the whole consolidated Act for "REGON" and "Krajowym Rejestrze Sądowym" found zero occurrences inside art. 106e or its neighboring invoice-content articles (106a-106q) — neither is added as a scheme here on the strength of commercial habit alone.

notes: Poland (2026-09-13). Primary source: ustawa z dnia 11 marca 2004 r. o podatku od towarów i usług, read as the tekst jednolity gazetted at Dz.U. 2025 poz. 775 (https://dziennikustaw.gov.pl/D2025000077501.pdf), curl + `pdftotext -layout`, cross-checked against the next-newest tekst jednolity (Dz.U. 2024 poz. 361) where noted in the underlying research; isap.sejm.gov.pl was not used (Incapsula bot protection). Only ONE scheme is declared ("LEGAL_ID", i.e. NIP) — no separate "VAT" scheme is proposed: Polish invoice law's "numer, za pomocą którego podatnik/nabywca jest zidentyfikowany na potrzeby podatku" is the SAME number this catalog already models as LEGAL_ID for a domestic party, unlike France's or Portugal's own SIREN-vs-TVA / NIF-vs-VAT-prefix splits. `required: false` is a DELIBERATE, structural choice, not an under-statement of the law — see this scheme's own `notes` for why a single boolean cannot honestly represent both Poland's unconditional SELLER duty (art. 106e ust. 1 pkt 4) and its conditional BUYER duty (art. 106e ust. 1 pkt 5) given this catalog's `appliesTo` axis and this product's shared seller/buyer consumption path (`country-identifiers.ts`'s `resolveRequiredIdentifiers`, `onboarding.tsx`, `company.settings.tsx`, `client-upsert.tsx` — all read before writing this file). DELIBERATELY NOT ENCODED, reported instead: (1) the buyer-side conditional half of pkt 5 — see this scheme's own `notes`, folded in rather than given a separate `unverified` fact because Poland has no second, distinctly-named identifier to host one under (contrast Italy's Codice Fiscale, which does get its own fact in it.json). (2) A KSeF-specific routing identifier for the buyer — established NOT to exist: art. 106gb ust. 4 i ust. 5 (formerly art. 106nc in the 2024-vintage text) shows a domestic, actively-registered VAT taxpayer's KSeF delivery resolves automatically off their own NIP (no second identifier), and the four carved-out buyer classes (foreign, no Polish establishment, an uninvolved Polish fixed establishment, or a small-business-exemption taxpayer under art. 113a) fall back to "made available in a manner agreed with the buyer" secured by a PER-INVOICE access/verification code (ust. 5), not a persistent per-party routing identifier comparable to Italy's Codice Destinatario — so no third scheme is needed for Poland's KSeF channel, it rides entirely on the NIP already modeled here. (3) The PESEL alternative for a non-VAT-registered INDIVIDUAL seller (ustawa o zasadach ewidencji i identyfikacji podatników i płatników, art. 3 ust. 1 pkt 1 i ust. 1a) — reported in this scheme's own `notes`; this catalog has no PESEL scheme and `appliesTo` is kept `'COMPANY'`-only for exactly this reason, rather than `'BOTH'` with a wrong label for some individual sellers. OPEN QUESTIONS NOT RESOLVED BY THIS PASS (see the underlying research file for the full list): whether a non-VAT-registered Polish COMPANY (as opposed to an individual) still holds and must state a NIP at all — the identification Act's PESEL/NIP branch is drafted specifically for natural-person taxpayers, and this task did not chase whether a non-VAT-registered legal person can issue a `faktura VAT` under this Act in the first place; the exact NIP character format (10-digit numeric is the widely-known convention, not chased to a primary-text statement in either statute read here — no `pattern` is declared for that reason).
